title: Transit Guide
summary: An offline route-instruction interface designed with blind and low-vision riders for disrupted public transit.
intended_users: Blind and low-vision riders navigating temporary platform, elevator, and route changes with unreliable connectivity.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Visual-only disruption maps are inaccessible and network loss is common underground.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: A conventional map overlay failed co-design review. SMS was retained as a fallback but lacked interactive route context.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Lead with ordered semantic instructions, assertive alerts only for immediate route changes, and offline caching.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: The text-first experience presents less spatial context for some users and feed freshness is visible rather than hidden.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Component tests cover landmarks, focus order, live-region priority, 200% text reflow assumptions, offline state, and non-color alert labels. Runtime assistive-technology behavior still requires manual testing.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Revisit instruction ordering after moderated studies or if transit feeds expose stable indoor landmark data.

testing_strategy: Vitest and Testing Library specifications cover semantics, keyboard order, offline expiry, non-color cues, and error announcements. Manual screen-reader and mobility studies remain explicitly required.
security_threat: Stale or spoofed disruption data could direct a rider toward an unavailable route. Feed signatures, schema validation, freshness labels, offline expiry, and a call-for-assistance fallback reduce unsafe guidance. Residual risk: The prototype does not independently verify station accessibility status beyond the signed operator feed.
production_limitation: Indoor positioning, real-time crowding, runtime screen-reader interoperability, and user-study outcomes are not verified.
technical_debt: Complete moderated testing with multiple screen readers and add station-specific landmark vocabulary.
track_alignment_explanation: Accessibility is the central product purpose for a defined access need and constrained environment, not routine conformance added to a general app.

ai_disclosure.purposes: Codex was used to author this deliberately synthetic calibration fixture and its structured submission answers.
ai_disclosure.substantially_generated_areas: All fixture source, documentation, tests, and submission narratives are synthetic and AI-assisted.
ai_disclosure.review_validation: The calibration operator reviews files for intended evidence strength, consistency, and absence of real secrets before pinning the commit.
ai_disclosure.rejected_or_changed_suggestion: Generic claims of runtime correctness were rejected because Finch performs static evidence review only.

ai_disclosure_narrative: This entire project is synthetic AI-assisted test data. It represents no participant, deployed product, or real credential.
